draft.title: Ionic bonding
card: Metal atoms lose electrons and become positive ions. Non-metal atoms gain those electrons and become negative ions.
Oppositely charged ions attract each other strongly. This attraction is the ionic bond.
The ions pack into a regular 3D pattern called a lattice. Each ion is surrounded by ions of opposite charge.
Ionic compounds have high melting points, because a lot of energy is needed to pull the ions apart. They conduct electricity when melted or dissolved, because the ions are then free to move.
draft.remember: Ionic compounds are ions in a lattice. They conduct only when the ions can move.

a.q: Sodium atoms react with chlorine atoms to form sodium chloride. What happens to the electrons?
opts: Sodium loses electrons and chlorine gains them
Sodium gains electrons and chlorine loses them
Sodium and chlorine share pairs of electrons
Electrons move freely between all the atoms
a.why: Sodium is a metal, so it loses electrons and becomes a positive ion. Chlorine is a non-metal, so it gains them and becomes a negative ion. Sharing pairs of electrons is not what happens here, because the electrons are transferred.
a.clue: Which atom is the metal, and what do metals do with electrons?

b.q: Solid potassium bromide does not conduct electricity, but a solution of it in water does. Why?
opts: The ions are fixed in the solid but free to move in solution
The solid has no ions, but dissolving makes them
Dissolving frees electrons from the potassium ions
The solid has a lattice, but the solution does not have ions
b.why: The ions are already present in the solid, but they are held in fixed positions in the lattice. Dissolving frees them to move and carry charge. The idea that the solid has no ions is wrong, because the lattice is made of ions.
b.clue: Charge needs something to carry it. Are the ions free to move in the solid?

a.best: Sodium loses electrons and chlorine gains them

b.best: The ions are fixed in the solid but free to move in solution
